turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Okay, let's get started. Thanks for joining, Marcus. Today I want to settle three things: the vendor decision, the migration date, and who owns the rollback plan.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Sounds good. I read the proposal from Northwind Systems last night. The headline number is $48,500 a year, down from the $62,000 we pay Halvorsen today.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: That's a saving of $13,500, which is about twenty-two percent. Does that include the SOC 2 audit support, or is that an add-on?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: It's an add-on. The audit package is another $9,200, but Priya Ramanathan from compliance says we need it either way, so I'd treat the real saving as $4,300.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Fair. Even so, I'd rather negotiate from there than stay put. What did you find on uptime? Last quarter Halvorsen missed their SLA twice.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Northwind commits to 99.95 percent, with service credits starting at 10 percent of the monthly fee. In their reference calls, nobody reported an outage longer than forty minutes.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Good. And the API? Our reconciliation job calls the billing API roughly 40,000 times a night, so rate limits matter more than the logo on the invoice.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: That was my worry too. Their default limit is 25 requests per second per key, and we can request 100 for the same price. I'd ask for that in writing.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Agreed, put it in the contract. Now, the migration date. Engineering wanted March 14th, but that's the week the finance team closes the quarter.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Right, and Tomasz in finance was clear that he doesn't want any change to invoicing during close. If we slip to March 28th, we avoid that entirely.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Two weeks later costs us about $2,100 in extra Halvorsen fees, but a failed close would cost far more. I'm comfortable with March 28th.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Then the plan is a dual-run from March 14th, where both systems process invoices, and a cutover on the 28th once the totals match for five consecutive days.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Five days feels short. Let's say ten business days of matching totals, with a tolerance of one cent per invoice.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Ten days it is. Which brings us to the rollback plan. Whoever owns it needs access to both vendors' dashboards and the authority to call it.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: I'd like that to be Ingrid. She ran the last cutover, she knows the Kubernetes jobs, and she isn't afraid to stop a release at two in the morning.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: She's the right person. I'll write up the runbook with her this week: triggers, the exact commands, and a decision point at 6 a.m. Lisbon time.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Why Lisbon time?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Because the nightly batch finishes around 5:40 a.m. there, and that's before the Lisbon support team starts their shift. We need a human awake who can say yes or no.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Understood. Budget-wise, let me confirm: $48,500 license, $9,200 audit package, plus roughly $6,000 for the migration contractors. That's $63,700 in year one.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Correct, and that's still under the $75,000 that the steering committee approved in January. The EBITDA impact is small but positive from year two.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: One more thing on cost. Do we need to pay for the sandbox environment separately?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Yes, it's $400 a month, but they waive it for the first six months if we sign before the end of February. I'll make sure that goes into the redlines.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Good. What are the risks you'd put on the slide for Thursday?

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Three. One, data mapping errors in legacy invoices from before 2019. Two, the contractors' availability in March. Three, Northwind's sandbox is sometimes slower than production, which hides performance problems.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: I'd add a fourth: our own staff attention. Everyone is also preparing for the audit in April.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: True. I'll add it, and I'll propose a freeze on non-essential releases from March 10th through the 31st.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: And training? Last time we lost three days because nobody on support knew how to read the new reports.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Northwind includes two live sessions. I'd book them for the week of March 17th, so the support team has real invoices to practise on during the dual-run.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Good. Make sure the Lisbon team is invited, not just the head office.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Of course. I'll also ask for recordings, so new hires can watch them later.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Do that. Last item: who tells Halvorsen? They'll want to renegotiate, and I'd like to be the one on the call.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: I'd suggest you wait until the contract with Northwind is signed. Otherwise they'll know we have no alternative ready and dig in.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Sensible. Let's target signature by February 21st, then the call with Halvorsen the following Monday.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: I'll send Northwind our redlines tomorrow. Their legal contact is Beatriz Kowalczyk, and she usually answers within a day.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Perfect. So, to recap: Northwind Systems at $48,500, audit package at $9,200, dual-run from March 14th, cutover March 28th, Ingrid owns rollback, signature by February 21st.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: That matches my notes. I'll circulate the summary within the hour.

turns.speaker: dana
turns.text: Thanks, Marcus. Talk Thursday.
